specification.title: Working Draft, Standard for Programming Language C++ (N4659)
specification.version: C++17 working draft N4659 (2017-03-21); accepted DRs named by tests separately

inventory.notes: Incomplete source-oriented C++17 feature inventory, not an official run-pass suite denominator. Supported rows describe bounded capabilities and retain their actually executed historical compiler revisions; matching source bytes do not qualify execution on a later integrated master. Only the constructor scalar-direct evidence triplet and passed entry were renewed from retained bdb execution to replace a stale unit-file binding; all other published evidence remains historical. New DMI/placement/cstddef/decltype/nullptr/SysV-varargs/postfix scopes do not establish native pcc1, full bootstrap, five-GC, NumPy or complete C++17 acceptance. Known external-reference failures and missing native prerequisites remain explicit below. Current unchanged TinyXML2 frontier is the in-class StrPair constructor and external-inline ODR; no owned project executable exists.

features.title: Non-inline non-static member functions through pointer receivers
features.scope: Bounded non-inherited/non-virtual classes: out-of-class definitions, arrow and implicit-this calls, const/non-const overloads, private access, object-before-argument evaluation and typed ABI. Twenty-three exact caller/method programs execute against independently supplied foreign object storage; a separate C++ reference provider supplies storage only. This does not qualify constructors, dot-receiver addresses, inline ODR, native pcc1, standalone projects or a private runtime. Same-source explicit G++ reference is not a production dependency. Independent ABI, two-TU and export tests are additionally recorded in the historical cb41 qualification, not counted as 26 independent executions. The 23 unchanged original inputs, fixtures and unit/runtime test functions were requalified on e816; all 46 exact node calls passed and all retained owned/reference executions were independently rechecked. Original cb41 records remain in published Git history, not relabeled as recovered artifacts.

features.title: Class-template complete-object D1 ownership, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for primary destructor MethodPatterns, concrete D1 declarations, access-checked automatic destruction-use requests, FIFO external-ODR emission and the shared normal-exit cleanup/proof owner. Dependent delete retains typed syntax and fails at actual use without owned deallocation. Explicit D1 without a bound proof, nested unbound template cleanup, local class/reference/array replay, allocating new/delete and original DynArray/TinyXML2 acceptance remain unqualified.

features.title: Class-template self-reference copy declarations, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for declaration-only self lvalue-reference copy constructors and assignment members, injected-to-concrete referent identity, const and access preservation, per-specialization C1/assignment mangling and address ABI. No implicit copy overload or body is fabricated. Selected private constructors fail access before scheduling; public unavailable copy bodies fail explicitly. Copy definitions, assignment calls, generic reference-parameter Patterns and class-reference results remain boundaries. Also retains the exact CI-failed ordinary reference-returning operator[] and zero-argument dependent explicit-template-call programs through their existing semantic owners. Exact TinyXML2 private declaration excerpts do not establish original DynArray or project acceptance.

features.title: Dependent member array-new Patterns, awaiting validation
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for one-dimensional uninitialized array-new Patterns in class-template member bodies when allocated type or bound is dependent. Allocated type identity, integral first-bound expressions, definition-point local bindings and global lookup syntax are retained without token replay. First bounds may be runtime values or zero; known constant negative lengths are rejected independently of fixed-array bound rules. Concrete void/reference/incomplete/const-scalar restrictions and class-element lifetime gates are checked before any allocation lowering. Every odr-used new[] still fails before IR at the owned allocation/lookup/size/failure/initialization/deallocation boundary; no default allocator or successful allocation value is fabricated. Native positive observers execute only unrelated supported members or separate entry units, not allocation. Both formerly rejected unused-body original inputs are preserved unchanged. Function-template, scalar, nondependent, initialized, multidimensional, converted nonintegral and unevaluated new forms retain explicit gaps. Native pcc1 frontend, allocation runtime and unchanged TinyXML2 acceptance remain unqualified. No local tests, imports, compilers or collection were run.

features.title: Class-template body-local pointer/cv declarations, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for body-local object pointers and cv scalar/pointer declarations in class-template members, including definition-point symbol identity, dependent local const initialization checks, ordinary typed Pattern substitution/storage, pointer and pointee qualifiers, local shadowing, injected-class pointer identity, once-only subscript addresses, static members, full-width scalar storage, lazy unused bodies and cross-TU external-ODR identity. Function-template pointer/cv typing, volatile access, local class/array/reference lifetime, callbacks and allocation remain explicit boundaries. Exact TinyXML2 header local-declaration excerpts are preserved but do not establish unchanged PushArr, EnsureCapacity or project acceptance. No local tests, PCC imports, compiler runs or collection were performed; CI must establish every authored outcome. Native pcc1 frontend and complete C++17 remain unqualified.

features.title: First-declaration defaulted destructors, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for non-template first-declaration defaulted D1s, independent deletion/triviality/user-provided identity, recursive implicit-member deletion and access checks, and lazy emitted bodies through the existing exact member-cleanup proof and external-ODR worklist. Class completion classifies deletion before deferred default arguments and DMIs, including the unchanged deleted-D1 unevaluated default-argument counterexample. Unused declarations and valid unevaluated calls request no member body. Ordinary, placement, reverse-order, return, loop, nested-member, body-local and cross-TU original programs have authored owned-native/reference rows; no observed pass is claimed. The exact formerly rejected defaulted declaration is preserved unchanged as a positive original. Implicit nontrivial D1 synthesis, template/later defaulting, explicit exception specifications, class-array lifetimes, unknown destructor effects, unavailable evaluated-use bodies, bases/virtual dispatch, internal-linkage ownership and unwinding remain explicit boundaries. Native pcc1 frontend and unchanged TinyXML2 project acceptance remain unqualified. No local tests, imports, compilers or collection were run; CI must establish these outcomes.

acceptance.scope: Complete bounded first-declaration defaulted-D1 corpus, including all parametrized unit, owned-native, reference and rejection obligations
acceptance.reason: Source-only implementation and authored obligations; user delegated execution to CI. No unit, native program, external reference, collection or validator execution was performed. The revision identifies the immutable corrected source/test patch, not an executed compiler. Native pcc1 and unchanged TinyXML2 project acceptance remain unqualified.

features.title: Scalar/pointer array member semantics, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun source/owned-native/reference obligations for complete scalar/pointer array data members, natural target record layout and sticky size-overflow failures, nested explicit aggregate initialization and omitted/empty zero initialization, const-element deletion/mutability, defaulted-C1 zero prefixes, omitted constructor no-store plans, bounded explicit-empty constructor zero loops, trivial destruction, class-template array decay/subscripts, placement and explicit D1 reuse. No uninitialized scalar is read in the native corpus. Exact formerly rejected originals and TinyXML2 constructor/field excerpts are retained unchanged. Class-element arrays, array DMIs, braced constructor-array initialization, brace elision, function-template arrays, copy/move synthesis, heap allocation runtime, native pcc1 frontend and unchanged TinyXML2 project acceptance remain unqualified boundaries. No local tests, PCC imports, compilers or collection were run; CI must establish the authored outcomes.

features.title: Typed class-template constant array bounds, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for definition-point typed fixed and value-dependent class-template array bounds, integral non-type parameter identities, nested pointer-to-array substitution, target constant proofs, lazy completeness and sticky diagnostics. The exact previously rejected fixed-array primary declaration is retained unchanged as a positive declaration-only input. features.title: Shared natural-record and dependent sizeof queries, awaiting execution
features.scope: Authored, execution-unrun obligations for class storage queries using the same extracted natural-record calculation as C IR storage, target-owned scalar/alignment facts, one-byte empty-class projection, and typed dependent sizeof replay with no runtime operand or member-body use. features.title: Single non-virtual bases of non-polymorphic classes, with base construction and destruction
features.scope: One direct non-virtual base per class (public, protected or private), at offset 0 as a leading C field or, when empty, with no storage (Itanium empty-base optimization). Member lookup, unqualified names in member functions and C::m qualified lookup follow the base chain; access follows [class.access.base]/5 and [class.protected]. Derived-to-base pointer conversion and direct reference binding to the base subobject are admitted, ranked by [over.ics.rank]/4.4. sizeof includes the base field. A declared derived constructor constructs the base first (a Base(args) mem-initializer or default construction through a declared base constructor); that base constructor is access-checked as a member named through *this ([class.access.base]/5, [class.protected]), so a protected constructor, or one inherited through a private base, is accessible there while a separate base object in a derived member still is not (TinyXML2's XMLText : XMLNode(doc); five programs run natively on the Mac with owned arm64 compile/assemble/link and match Apple clang, which also rejects the three inaccessible uses; Linux execution unrun). a declared derived destructor destroys it after the members. Only layouts the natural C record reproduces exactly are admitted (a POD base, a base without tail padding, or a derived class without data members). Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list. A member-owning constructor called before its out-of-line definition in the same unit (TinyXML2's XMLText : XMLNode(doc)) defers its closed-construction proof to that body, as a class template instance does: the body proves or rejects it, and a unit that never binds it fails at the call. Three programs run natively on the Mac with owned arm64 compile/assemble/link and match Apple clang (Linux execution unrun), moving tinyxml2.cpp from tinyxml2.h:993:25 to 1695:17.

features.title: Overriding and virtual dispatch through a single polymorphic non-virtual base
features.scope: A dynamic single base is the Itanium primary base: the derived class shares its table pointer at offset 0 and its table holds the base entries with this class's final overriders in place, then its new virtual functions. Same-signature members override implicitly or with override/final, including destructors; overriding a final member, a different non-covariant return, a static overrider and override without an overridden member are ordinary errors. Covariant class pointer/reference returns need no adjustment at offset 0. Abstractness follows the final overriders. Declared constructors, and the implicitly declared or first-declaration defaulted default constructor of a non-template class, store the class table after base construction and before members; value-initialization zero-initializes the object before that constructor runs; every polymorphic destructor stores it on entry ([class.cdtor]/4). Unqualified and explicit destructor calls load the final overrider; qualified calls are direct. An empty non-dynamic base may sit under a new table pointer. Implicit or defaulted virtual destructors, implicit or defaulted constructors of class-template specializations or over a base with a user constructor, eager per-unit tables (an out-of-line virtual function must be defined in some linked unit even when no object is created), slicing copies, a nonempty non-dynamic base under a new table pointer and tail-padding reuse remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: A nondependent single base of a class template
features.scope: A class template may name one complete nondependent class as its non-virtual base ([temp.dep]/3 binds it at the definition). Every specialization shares it: the base is the leading C field or an empty base with no storage, implicit and declared constructors construct it first and destructors destroy it last, and member access, access checks and derived-to-base conversions use inheritance.py. Naming base members inside member bodies (unqualified or through this), mem-initializers naming the base, and dependent and template-id bases remain explicit gaps; a base that needs destruction is constructed under the closed-construction proof and polymorphic bases are covered by cpp.class-template-virtuals. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Virtual members and polymorphic bases of class templates
features.scope: Class template members may be declared virtual, override or final (including destructors and pure members) and may implicitly override a virtual member of a nondependent polymorphic base. A nondependent signature's override rules (target, final, return type, static) are checked at the definition, a dependent one by each specialization. Each specialization declares its overriders, owns its own table of final overriders (all of which are ODR-used) and stores it in its constructors and destructors; unqualified calls dispatch through it. Specialization constructors construct a base that needs destruction under the closed-construction proof. Defaulted and implicit virtual destructors, virtual operators and base members named inside member bodies remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Unnamed unscoped member enums of class templates
features.scope: An unnamed unscoped member enum of a class template keeps each enumerator initializer as a definition-point Pattern; an enumerator of the current instantiation is value-dependent when its initializer is. Each specialization builds its own enum with the ordinary owner (values, implicit successors, fixed or selected underlying type and range checks) before its members, so member bodies, array bounds, member access and S<N>::K name that specialization's enumerators, with member access control. Named and scoped member enums of class templates and enum object declarators remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Non-inline static data members of non-template classes
features.scope: Non-inline static data members of non-template classes: the in-class declaration declares one external object (Itanium _ZN..E) under the member's access; one namespace-scope definition T C::m = init; defines it, with its initializer looked up and access-checked in the class scope and initialized by the shared static initialization owner (constants, zero, null, object addresses, and string literals for const char pointers, also admitted for namespace objects). Simple and qualified names, assignments, addresses and x.m / p->m (base evaluated, then the static object) work across translation units; redefinition, type mismatch, undeclared members, repeated storage, private access and member conflicts are ordinary errors. features.title: Unions with trivial members
features.scope: A union is a class whose non-static data members share offset 0, projected to the shared C union record; size and alignment are the largest member's (rounded). Only members whose special members are all trivial are admitted (scalars, pointers, enums, arrays of them, trivial classes and unions), so the union's implicit special members are trivial. A braced list initializes the first member; value-initialization zeroes it. Both require the first member to cover the union, because zeroed padding must be real. A base clause, a virtual function and a class-key that disagrees with an earlier declaration are ordinary errors. Union member functions, constructors, destructors, friends, static members, default member initializers, non-trivial members, anonymous unions and list-initialization of a union whose first member is smaller than the union remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Unions — remaining capability boundary
features.scope: Only inputs routed to cpp.unsupported.unions in the pinned frontend (non-trivial union members and list-initialization of a union whose first member is smaller than the union); the trivial-member subset is cpp.unions.

features.title: Data-only member classes and unions of class templates
features.scope: A struct, class or union defined inside a class template with data members only is a dependent member class of the current instantiation. Each specialization builds its own class before its own members, with a C tag unique to the specialization and an Itanium nested-name under the specialization (substitution candidates included); member types substitute the enclosing parameters, member enumerators and earlier member classes, including dependent array bounds. Member bodies may access public data members of a member class through objects, pointers and array elements. Arrays of, and by-value members of, a member class whose special members are all trivial need no construction or destruction; an array needs destruction exactly when its element does. Member functions, bases, nested declarations and default member initializers inside member classes, non-public member access from member bodies, and naming Outer<args>::Member outside the template remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Dependent template-id members, current-instantiation names and non-throwing destructor bodies
features.scope: A class template data member whose type is a class template-id with dependent type arguments (DynArray<Block*, 10>) is a TemplateIdPattern: each specialization substitutes the arguments and names the shared specialization, which its constructors and destructors construct and destroy like any class member. Member calls and data member access on such an object are looked up in the concrete class when the body is instantiated. Name<P1, ..., Pn>:: with the primary template's own parameter names, and qualified lookup through the injected-class-name, denote the current instantiation, so its member calls are direct calls on this. A template constructor's closed-construction proof becomes an obligation checked when its body is instantiated. Every admitted destructor has the implicit non-throwing exception specification (explicit specifications are rejected), so an unknown call in a destructor body needs no member cleanup path; the unproven body stays recorded as not closed for placement and explicit-destruction owners. Value-dependent value arguments, dependent template-ids in member function signatures and naming other specializations' members remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Allocating new/delete over the global replaceable allocation functions
features.scope: new T, new T() and new T(args) call operator new(sizeof(T)) (_Znwm) and then initialize: a declared constructor through the shared C1 owner, a class whose special members are all trivial by nothing or by value-initialization, a scalar by nothing, zero or the converted argument. new E[n] for trivially destructible E (no cookie) calls operator new[](n*sizeof(E)), passing SIZE_MAX when the size overflows or n is negative so allocation fails. delete p destroys a non-null complete object through its D1 and calls the sized operator delete (_ZdlPvm, [expr.delete]/10); delete[] p calls the unsized operator delete[] (_ZdaPv). Class template members keep typed new-object/new-array/delete Patterns that lower at instantiation after re-checking the substituted types and counts. Every translation unit implicitly declares the usual functions; programs may replace the usual unaligned forms, and C++ executables link owned weak defaults over malloc/free/abort whose array and sized forms forward as the defaults do (default-allocator execution is unrun: it needs the owned runtime). Allocation failure terminates (no exception support). Class-specific allocation functions, aligned and nothrow forms, braced and initialized-array new-initializers, multidimensional array-new, class elements with lifetimes and deleting a polymorphic object remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: static_cast in class template member bodies
features.scope: Inside a class template member body, static_cast keeps a typed static-cast Pattern (target type and operand); instantiation applies the ordinary static_cast rules to the substituted types, including arithmetic conversions and the cv void* to object pointer conversion (TinyXML2 MemPoolT::Free). Invalid substituted casts (removing const from the pointee) are ordinary errors at instantiation. Casts in function templates and the other static_cast kinds keep their existing explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.

features.title: Ordinary string literals as const char[N] lvalues
features.scope: An ordinary string literal (and a sequence of adjacent ones) is an lvalue of type const char[N] whose bytes are decoded in phase 6 before concatenation: simple, octal and hexadecimal escapes (each must fit an unsigned char), universal-character-names and non-basic source characters encoded as UTF-8. The decoded bytes are re-spelled with three-digit octal escapes for the shared C owner. Literals in class template member bodies are typed Patterns; a member may pass one to a non-template function, whose array argument decays without deduction. Prefixed (L, u, U, u8) and raw literals and conditionally-supported escapes remain explicit gaps. Source revision is sha256 of the sorted compact JSON source list.
